title: CLI regression: ToolContext ImportError breaks every browser-tool agent (web-retriever, solutions-architect, experience-architect)
description: In installed CLI v1.0.65, spruce_grove/tools/browser/browser_control.py does `from spruce_grove.harness import ToolContext`, which raises ImportError (ToolContext not exported from spruce_grove.harness). Because agent tool registration imports browser tools unconditionally, EVERY agent whose toolset includes browser tools fails to start: web-retriever, solutions-architect, experience-architect all died on invoke. Impact: subagent delegation is effectively down for research/architecture agents. Repro: invoke any of those agents. Fix: export ToolContext from spruce_grove.harness, or make browser_control import lazy/guarded. Worked around this session by doing the work inline.
close_reason:
FIXED in the CLI. Root cause was NOT a v1.0.65 regression: the ToolContext export and the browser_control import landed together in v1.0.69, so no released version was internally inconsistent. The real cause was a stale in-process module -- a CLI started 18:04 held a pre-upgrade spruce_grove.harness after the 09:29 install, so the lazy import failed.

Fixed + pushed in the CLI repo: 8d74d2d makes one failing tool non-fatal in register_tools_for_agent (so a broken browser tool can never kill delegation again), and the lazy ToolContext binding now raises an ImportError that names the stale-process cause and the restart fix.

The systemic root cause (self-update invalidating a running process's module table) is tracked in the CLI repo as the bead 'Stale in-process modules after self-update'. Workaround until then: restart the CLI after any upgrade. Verified: subset suite 7929 passed, 41 skipped in the CLI repo.

title: Packaged CSP blocked data: images (look-in panel dead in shipped builds)
description: Surfaced during the leave-no-stone-unturned sweep (2026-09-22): tauri.conf.json CSP was still the pre-REVIEW value (default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'), which blocks data: images — the look-in panel's screenshots and workspace shell.json logos render broken in the packaged app while the Playwright harness (no CSP) passed. Fixed: default-src 'self'; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'. Guard: the UI harness now serves every response under the packaged CSP (script-src 'unsafe-inline' added only for the injected mock bridge), so this bug class fails in CI instead of shipping.

close_reason: Fixed: aria-labels on all icon-only controls (sidebar-toggle/open, insp-refresh/close, picker up/close, persona radio/name/remove/dirs, cwd, cancel, prompt); #status is role=status aria-live=polite; transcript is role=log with live off (no token-stream flooding); inspector tabs are a real tablist/tab/tabpanel with arrow-key walking and aria-selected; settings dialog moves focus in on open and restores the invoker on close; picker restores invoker focus; inspector toggle carries aria-pressed. All asserted in UI suite section 15.

title: Self-host webfonts: app + deck silently degrade offline
description: Google Fonts (Fraunces, EB Garamond, IM Fell English SC, JetBrains Mono, Inter) load from fonts.googleapis.com at runtime. QA swarm observed the css2 request fail (status 0) and type fall back mid-app; the transcript's display face changes the moment streaming renders. Demo venues have flaky wifi. Fix: vendor the woff2 files + @font-face locally for ui/ and handoff/.
close_reason: Fixed: all five families self-hosted — 11 woff2 files in ui/fonts/ (variable-weight ranges: Fraunces 400-600 incl. opsz, Inter 400-600, JetBrains Mono 400-600, EB Garamond 400-500 normal+italic, IM Fell 400; latin + latin-ext), ui/fonts.css with real @font-face rules, Google links removed from ui/index.html and all three handoff decks (handoff/fonts.css + handoff/fonts/). Zero network at runtime; CSP-clean; offline cannot degrade the transcript's type mid-stream. tools/vendor-fonts.py re-vendors reproducibly (652KB per side).

title: Sidebar session-row UX pack: phantom row, stale active highlight, nested destructive x
description: Swarm findings: (1) upsertSession(res.sessionId, cwd, 'new session') runs on every startAcp incl. boot auto-start, so every launch re-stamps a 'new session . now' row the user never created; (2) after New chat the old session keeps the active highlight while you view the new one; (3) the forget-session x button (17x18px, below WCAG 2.5.8 target size) is nested inside the clickable row used to resume - accidental demo-data deletion risk; nested interactive elements are also invalid HTML.
close_reason: Fixed all three: (1) startAcp no longer stamps a 'new session' row — row creation now requires an explicit create flag, passed only by newChat; boot auto-start, dir switches, resumes and self-heals touch no rows, and sendPrompt records the session with its real first prompt. (2) startAcp clears activeSessionId and re-renders up front, so slow/failed starts cannot leave a stale ember highlight; the old pre-sets in openSession/newChat are gone. (3) session rows are role=button divs (aria-label, tabindex, Enter/Space activation, aria-current) so the destructive × is a real button, not a button nested in a button.

title: QA-kitten screenshot media uploads time out; require DOM-only constraint
description: Twice this session a qa-kitten run died with ModelHTTPError 400 uploading screenshot media (files.synthetic.new timed out), and one retry produced a report describing deck content that does not exist (hallucinated after truncated instructions). Lessons: (1) always pass an explicit no-screenshots/DOM-only constraint for qa-kitten runs; (2) never accept agent reports of content not asserted against a manifest; (3) prefer deterministic Playwright extraction scripts (see /tmp/deck_extract.py pattern) for content ground-truth over LLM narration.
close_reason: Fixed: qa-kitten SKILL.md gained an 'Evidence Transport Constraint (this rig)' section — (1) never upload screenshot media to the model (files.synthetic.new times out with ModelHTTPError 400 and kills the run; evidence must travel as DOM text: snapshots, computed styles, bounding boxes), (2) never report from truncated instructions — stop and say so instead of hallucinating content (the deck-report incident). Updated the canonical plugin source (SPRUCE-GROVE-OS venv code_puppy_core_plugins/qa_kitten_skill) AND the deployed copy in ~/.code_puppy/plugin-skills/; both md5-verified identical.

title: Mock harness gaps: cancel does not stop fake stream; resume emits no replay
description: QA swarm observed cancel as a no-op and resume as a stuck 'Resuming...' placeholder - both are MOCK gaps, not app bugs (real backend sends session/cancel JSON-RPC and session/load replays correctly; cargo tests + acp_probe --lifecycle cover both). Improve tests/test_desktop_ui.py MOCK: grove_acp_cancel should halt the pending fake stream and emit a cancelled/turn-end; resume path should emit a replayed chunk so the UI placeholder is replaced. Then add a UI assertion for cancel feedback.
close_reason: Fixed in the MOCK (tests/test_desktop_ui.py), mirroring the real backend: grove_acp_cancel now stops the fake stream dead — all pending stream timers are cleared, a turn token guards against stragglers, and an orderly turn-end with stopReason 'cancelled' arrives 20ms later (long-tail turns ≥3 give cancel a real window instead of racing a 200ms end_turn). grove_acp_start with resume now emits a session/load replay as ordinary agent_message_chunk events, asserted in the UI suite. The mock is single-source for both the suite and tests/mock_server.py.
